project.name: dsasign
project.context: Next.js 16 App Router project for ElGamal/DSA-style key generation, signing, and verification.
project.runtimeConstraint: Next.js App Router on Node.js runtime
project.architectureConstraint: single-app architecture with route handlers and shared server crypto modules

keySignals: App Router routes exist for /keygen, /sign, and /verify
Shared crypto code already exists in src/lib
Tailwind-based component primitives are already installed
The landing page is still the create-next-app scaffold

designFlexibilityPolicy.tokenLockingRule: Semantic roles are required, but exact primitive values stay flexible until repo evidence, accessibility validation, implementation constraints, or explicit user approval locks them.

conceptualAnchor.specificReferencePoint: the flap seal, custody label, and stamped verification mark on a document envelope
conceptualAnchor.rationale: The product moves a document through a signer/verifier chain of custody, so an evidence envelope is a concrete artifact that naturally maps to sealed states, verification marks, and document identity.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMotion: seal the record, then confirm or reject it with a short, decisive stamp-like transition
conceptualAnchor.typographicDecision: use a readable sans-serif for explanation and Geist Mono for hashes, primes, and signature values so the evidence reads as data instead of decoration

motionRiskBudget.reducedMotion: replace the stamp-like transition with an instant state change and clear text update

typographyClusters.description: utility sans plus monospace code blocks, compact numerals, and no role contrast
typographyClusters.specificityEvidence: This reads like a developer tool that surfaces numbers and code, not a signer/verifier workflow.
typographyClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Technical web apps fall into this typography pattern when no stronger product anchor exists.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it turns the product into a console; DSASign needs explainers and math with explicit role contrast.

typographyClusters.description: neutral SaaS sans with every label and value at the same weight and size
typographyClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the standard admin-panel look that flattens meaning into evenly weighted form fields.
typographyClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Without intervention, product UIs often copy the generic SaaS hierarchy of one family and one weight.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it hides the distinction between instructions, hashes, keys, and results.

typographyClusters.description: editorial serif headline with tiny metadata and subdued data rows
typographyClusters.specificityEvidence: This resembles a reading product or article system more than an interactive signing tool.
typographyClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Projects that want authority often overcorrect into editorial serif styling.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because DSASign needs trust and clarity, not a literary facade.

paletteClusters.description: dark slate surface with one cyan accent and monochrome chrome
paletteClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the familiar dev-tool and terminal palette that erases document context.
paletteClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Technical apps default to dark neutral surfaces because they feel safe and legible.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the product should feel like evidence handling, not a terminal clone.

paletteClusters.description: gray-white admin surface with one blue accent and muted borders
paletteClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the common SaaS admin palette that makes every screen look interchangeable.
paletteClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Component kits often ship this as the default light theme.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the app needs a document-seal identity that survives renaming to another product.

paletteClusters.description: purple-blue gradient hero with glassy highlights and soft glow
paletteClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the standard AI-startup landing palette that turns every product into a mood board.
paletteClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Marketing and AI themes often drift into gradient spectacle when no domain anchor exists.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the product is a workflow, not a pitch deck.

layoutClusters.description: top nav plus three-card KPI row above a data table
layoutClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the generic SaaS admin layout that treats every task like reporting.
layoutClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Dashboard products are often composed from the same left-to-right hierarchy of cards and tables.
layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because DSASign is a guided custody flow, not a metrics console.

layoutClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the standard marketing site composition that sells a feature list instead of solving a task.
layoutClusters.categoryDefaultReason: New web products frequently begin with brochure structure by habit.
layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the first screen must move users into key generation, signing, or verification.

layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the app needs visible evidence, status, and explanation at the same time.

motionClusters.description: generic fade-and-slide transitions with no state-specific choreography

motionClusters.description: toast-only feedback with modal popups for every result
motionClusters.specificityEvidence: This is the common app fallback when no motion grammar is designed.
motionClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Teams often rely on notifications instead of stateful choreography.
motionClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the result needs to be visible in place on the document workflow surface.

imageryClusters.description: stock certificate or document photos as decorative hero art

imageryClusters.categoryDefaultReason: Products that mention security often drift into stock document photography.
imageryClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the product should show real interface states, not pretend paperwork.

imageryClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because the first viewport needs one concrete artifact reference to explain the workflow.

selectedCombination.hierarchy: stacked steps with one dominant panel

uncomfortableCombination.combinationLabel: ledger strip with side annotations + compact density + quiet serif labels
uncomfortableCombination.discomfortReason: It risks feeling too formal and too dense for a web app at first glance.
uncomfortableCombination.productLogicJustification: The discomfort is useful because the product is literally about proving custody and validity. A more formal layout makes the signature and verification state feel consequential instead of playful.

candidates.jobFit: Matches the signer/verifier workflow because a document is carried, sealed, and checked for tampering.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: One dominant document panel with a visible seal state and supporting custody metadata.
candidates.densityImplication: Medium density with enough metadata to make the state believable but not so much that the seal is lost.
candidates.typeImplication: Readable sans for instructions, monospace for hashes, primes, and signature values.
candidates.motionImplication: A short stamp-like transition when the envelope is sealed or rejected.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Generic dashboard chrome, brochure layouts, and decorative security icon wallpaper.

candidates.jobFit: Maps well to signing because the action is authoritative and produces a visible mark.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: A strong primary action and a result surface that feels pressed into place.
candidates.densityImplication: Dense enough to show math, but with a ceremonial pause around the result.
candidates.typeImplication: Data in mono, explanation in sans, with emphatic numerals for signature output.
candidates.motionImplication: The result should land with compression and release rather than drifting in.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Fuzzy onboarding copy, generic hero layouts, and too-soft notification-only feedback.

candidates.jobFit: Works because the app needs to preserve identity, origin, and verification metadata as a record.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: Metadata can sit beside the document in a tidy accession-style frame.
candidates.densityImplication: Lower density than the selected anchor, with careful labeling and catalog structure.
candidates.typeImplication: Serif or sans labels can be paired with tabular numerals for record fields.
candidates.motionImplication: A record can slip into an archive slot when verified.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Brochure tropes, marketing imagery, and decorative security symbols.

candidates.jobFit: Useful because each upload moves through a declared set of contents and an inspection step.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: A manifest strip for contents, a main document area, and a clear inspection outcome.
candidates.densityImplication: Moderate-to-high density because the workflow needs declared fields and verification state.
candidates.typeImplication: Monospace for declared values, sans for instructions, strong numerals for key parameters.
candidates.motionImplication: Inspection should feel like a brief check, not a lingering animation.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Abstract brand art and overly playful upload metaphors.

candidates.jobFit: Fits because the app is a readable record of who signed what and whether the signature still matches.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: A ledger spine with clear sections for key generation, signing, and verification.
candidates.densityImplication: Compact but structured, with room for notes, hashes, and step-by-step values.
candidates.typeImplication: A data-friendly sans and mono pairing with tabular numerals.
candidates.motionImplication: A page-like turn is acceptable for route changes, but the state update itself should be brisk.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Floating-card UI, glassmorphism, and decorative gradients.

finalAnchorContract.name: tamper-evident evidence envelope
finalAnchorContract.specificReferencePoint: the flap seal, custody label, and stamped verification mark on a document envelope
finalAnchorContract.rationale: The workflow is a proof-of-integrity journey, so a sealable evidence envelope gives the UI a concrete structure for document, key, signature, and verification states.
finalAnchorContract.signatureMotion: seal, verify, and reject with short stamp-like transitions
finalAnchorContract.typographicDecision: use readable sans for explanation and Geist Mono for hashes, parameters, and signatures

derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Use archive-like surfaces, deep ink text, verification green, warning amber, and rejection red because the anchor is a sealed evidence artifact rather than a brochure or dashboard.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Use ledger spacing with 8px multiples and slightly wider gaps around state and evidence sections so the envelope contents stay legible.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Use a sans/mono split so human instructions read separately from cryptographic values.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Use seal-like transitions and brief confirmation motion to mirror the act of stamping or rejecting an envelope.
derivedTokenLogic.colorSpace: OKLCH for new tokens, with existing token formats preserved where the repo already uses them.
derivedTokenLogic.spatialBaseUnit: 8px base with 16px, 24px, 32px, and 48px multiples for evidence spacing.
derivedTokenLogic.typeScaleMethod: fluid clamp() scale with a stronger role contrast between labels, instructions, and numeric data.
derivedTokenLogic.motionBudget: short micro-interactions, bounded layout shifts, and reduced-motion replacements for all confirmation states.
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Every semantic token role must trace to anchorReference; exact primitives stay flexible unless repo evidence, accessibility, implementation constraints, or explicit user approval locks them.

motionRiskBudget.reducedMotion: instant state change with clear textual confirmation

sourceFreshness.oldSourcePolicy: older sources may support durable principles only when labeled old-timeless; they cannot prove current-year modernity
sourceFreshness.userConceptAdaptation: Treat the repo brief as the first-class constraint and support it with evidence; do not replace it with a trend default.

evidenceTable.claim: The app is a Next.js App Router project with route handlers and shared crypto modules.
evidenceTable.decisionImpact: Confirms the single-app architecture and route-based UI/API flow.

evidenceTable.claim: The project brief requires key generation, signing, verification, and an education mode that exposes steps.
evidenceTable.decisionImpact: Locks the workflow and the need for visible math explanations.

motionPaletteDecision.densityDecisionSource: Use medium-high density because the workflow needs document state, keys, and math visible at once.
motionPaletteDecision.spatialDecision: Do not use 3D/canvas by default; the replacement interaction quality is crisp state transitions, visible evidence rails, and stamped verification feedback.

aiSafeUiAudit.failureDefinition: AI-safe UI uses template cards, generic marks, decorative grid or line wallpaper, calibration-mark wallpaper, placeholder copy, terminal-only user paths, safe palettes, glow backgrounds, or copied scaffold composition.
aiSafeUiAudit.interchangeabilityTest: If this UI can be renamed from dsasign to another product category without changing composition, palette, iconography, and motion, revise it.
aiSafeUiAudit.paletteExplorationRule: Use a visually exploratory product-derived palette with WCAG contrast and status clarity.
aiSafeUiAudit.backgroundPatternRule: Background marks must serve a named product function; never use grid, line, or calibration-mark backgrounds as first-output filler.

aiColorAudit.failureDefinition: AI color drift uses safe defaults before deriving roles from the product anchor.
aiColorAudit.reviewQuestion: Why does this palette belong to this product?

motionSpatialCourageAudit.defaultStance: Treat motion, scroll choreography, canvas, WebGL, and 3D as first-class options when they help the product.
motionSpatialCourageAudit.rejectionRule: State a product reason and replacement interaction quality before omitting 3D/canvas.
motionSpatialCourageAudit.reviewQuestion: Is the interaction as expressive as the product can responsibly support?

productionContentPolicy.userFacingCopyRule: Visible UI copy must be product-ready and task-specific. Do not ship testing, demo, sample, placeholder, lorem, TODO, coming soon, or scaffold labels unless they are real product states.
productionContentPolicy.terminalDependencyRule: User-facing workflows must be operable through the UI unless the product is explicitly a CLI, developer tool, or operational runbook.
productionContentPolicy.reviewQuestion: Can this UI be shipped to real users without removing test/demo copy or terminal-only workflow dependencies?

libraryDecisions.library: existing Next.js / React / Tailwind / shadcn-style primitives
libraryDecisions.purpose: Use the installed stack and refine the visual language around the product anchor instead of adding new framework layers.
libraryDecisions.fallbackIfUnavailable: Use native CSS, browser APIs, or existing dependencies.
libraryDecisions.selectionPolicy: Do not default to shadcn, native-only, Tailwind-only, or dependency avoidance by habit; choose only what fits the product.
libraryDecisions.officialScaffolderPolicy: For fresh projects, prefer official setup commands when they create the supported project shape.
libraryDecisions.frameworkNeutralityPolicy: Next.js, Vite, Astro, React Router, SvelteKit, Laravel, and plain HTML are candidates, not defaults or forbidden choices.

tokenLockingPolicy.promotionRule: Promote flexible tokens to locked only when user approval, repo evidence, accessibility validation, or implementation constraints require it.

colorTruth.intent: Choose semantic palette roles from the product context, repo evidence, and accessibility. Reject scaffold or SaaS palette defaults.

mutationRules.mobile: Prioritize the first decisive action and collapse support content into stacked sections.
mutationRules.tablet: Regroup the three flows instead of shrinking desktop.
mutationRules.desktop: Use space for hierarchy and scanability; avoid equal-weight modules without evidence.

motionSystem.purpose: Use expressive motion when it improves hierarchy, continuity, feedback, memorability, or confidence.

viewportBehavior.mobile: Recompose for touch, task priority, and constrained attention.
viewportBehavior.tablet: Regroup surfaces for medium width without cloning desktop or mobile.
viewportBehavior.desktop: Use space for hierarchy and scanability; avoid template grids.

designExecutionHandoff.primaryExperienceGoal: Define the main web application journey for dsasign from repo evidence, brief, and docs.

surfacePlan.goal: Move the user into key generation, signing, or verification quickly.
Show prime search, key material, and export affordances.
Upload a document, sign it, and surface the resulting signature.
Upload the document, signature, and public key, then expose the verification decision.

mobile.rationale: Prioritize the active workflow and keep the math legible in one column.

tablet.rationale: Use a split between action and evidence rather than a shrunken desktop.

desktop.rationale: Use width for explanation, steps, and export state without losing the main action.

designExecutionHandoff.taskFlowNarrative: The user starts with route selection, performs the core action, and then reads the evidence and outcome in place.
designExecutionHandoff.signatureMoveRationale: The signature move is the seal-like confirmation state that makes signing and verification feel deliberate instead of transactional.

driftSignals: single spinner for every loading state
icon wallpaper instead of product evidence
reviewRubric.failureTest: If the screen can be renamed to a different product without changing hierarchy, palette behavior, motion language, and state grammar, it has drifted.
reviewRubric.accessibilityGate: Focus, keyboard, contrast, status messaging, and target size failures block completion.

rules: Use repo evidence and the current brief first.
Do not copy layout rhythm or palette from external examples without product-fit rationale.
